metadata.case_name: LAM KWOK LING v. LAM KWOK WING AND OTHERS

injuries.description: fracture of the right distal radius
source: was diagnosed with a fracture of the right distal radius.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of lower end of radius, unspecified

source: He was diagnosed with De Quervain tenosynovitis, or the De Quervain syndrome.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of extensor muscle, fascia or tendon of thumb at wrist or hand level

manifestations.description: Swelling and tenderness over the right wrist
Limited movement and stiffness of the wrist
Spasm in right thumb and index finger when gripping
Residual pain in the right wrist limiting ability to use heavy implements and to play badminton
Positive Finkelstein's test suggestive of De Quervain's syndrome
Passed out for about 10 seconds after head hit the ground

treatments_received.treatment: Right wrist set in a plaster cast (cast removed 28 August 2008)
source: His right wrist was set in a plaster cast which was taken off on 28 August 2008.
He was given physiotherapy treatment at the end of which he still complained of residual pain over the right thumb, which was a complication related to the fracture.

treatments_received.treatment: Referral to Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology
source: Since there was no further improvement, he was referred to the Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology.

treatments_received.treatment: Analgesics and occupational therapy including a working splint (18 November 2009 to 5 January 2010)
source: He was given analgesics and occupational therapy treatment from 18 November 2009 to 5 January 2010 by way of a working splint which he wore in the daytime.

treatments_received.treatment: Consultation with psychiatrist (Dr Lam Tat Chung) on 8 occasions
source: he was referred to a specialist in psychiatry Dr Lam Tat Chung whom the plaintiff consulted on 8 occasions.
Dr Tio ... suggesting that one or two steroid injections should be considered (which the plaintiff had previously refused)

treatments_future.treatment: Surgical decompression / release of the overreactive thickened fibrous flexor sheath (considered in occasional cases)
source: In occasional cases when pain persists, surgery with release of the overreactive thickening of the fibrous flexor sheath (which causes the syndrome) is the treatment of choice.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Unable to play badminton (favourite sport) and football as before due to residual wrist pain
Unable to return to pre-accident carpentry/formwork work and has lost confidence in construction work
